per_option_rationale.rationale: Treated the derivative of -2x as +2 (sign error in applying power rule): f'(1) = 12+6+2 = 20.

Forgot to apply the power rule multiplier to the first two terms, computing f'(x) = 4x^2 + 3x - 2 as if the original exponents stayed unchanged, then evaluated at x=1: 4+3+(-2) = 5, then added the constant 5, giving 10.
Evaluated f(0) = 5 (the constant term) believing the derivative at any point equals the constant term of the polynomial.

explanation: Applying the power rule term by term: d/dx(4x^3) = 12x^2, d/dx(3x^2) = 6x, d/dx(-2x) = -2, d/dx(5) = 0. So f'(x) = 12x^2 + 6x - 2. Substituting x=1: 12+6-2 = 16.

explanation_sections.punchline: Differentiate each term using the power rule d/dx(ax^n) = nax^(n-1), then substitute x=1.
explanation_sections.approach: Derivation plan: apply power rule to each term separately. 4x^3 -> 12x^2; 3x^2 -> 6x; -2x -> -2; constant 5 -> 0. Combine: f'(x) = 12x^2 + 6x - 2. Evaluate at x=1: 12+6-2 = 16.
explanation_sections.lesson: Power rule: d/dx(ax^n) = n*a*x^(n-1). The derivative of a constant is 0. Never change the sign of a term when differentiating unless a negative is introduced by the exponent.
explanation_sections.timing: Under 45 seconds. One pass of the power rule then substitute. Trap: sign errors on the -2x term or forgetting the constant term becomes 0.
